method: Each of the six actual source/model rows in the final SHA-bound paired sheet was personally displayed with view_image and compared. Changed subjects were reopened after their last export; no bounds or metadata substitute for this visual comparison.

entries.resolution: All six original/model pairs show the original hanging green scout beneath the dark bat, separate pink snout/ears and dusty rose scalloped wings. The generic mount was replaced with continuous body/neck, real wing shoulder/elbow/wrist and tarsal/claw anatomy. The whole goblin torso, arms and legs sit within the actual brown suspension harness with tunic/skirt and crossed back straps; physical interfaces are separate measured evidence.

All six pairs show the blood bat's dark red body, pink snout, torn red membranes and green red-haired rider. Source red shoulder shells/spikes, brown fitted vest/back straps and forked whole gripped polearm are present. Actual continuous body, real bones/membranes, anatomical hind joints and whole seated upper-body/hips replace disconnected generic forms.

All six pairs show the grey bloodwolf with separate pointed red brow/cheek/neck harness and dorsal/crupper tack, dark paw claws and bushy curled tail. Brown leather hood/front/rear vest, source red spiked pauldrons/wrist guards and irregular rusty red-edged cleaver replace the prior grey rider/flat pink brow/plain white weapon. Entire rider assembly is inclined over joined seated hips/thighs and source saddle rather than repositioned legs alone.

All six source/model pairs show the armored iron bat with dusty rose membranes, fitted metal forehead/cheek/belly and wing-root armor, anatomical hind paws and continuous closed body. The rider has the source rounded steel cap with continuous contacting temples/cheeks, steel front and brown leather rear layers, and the whole wood/metal crossbow held as one connected assembly. The source profile and structural features replace the former generic animal and exposed rider seams. The last source-equipment repair adds a real open leather rear quiver, steel rim bindings, three complete seated arrows with attached heads/fletching and actual measured quiver-to-body and arrow-to-base contacts; the new back gear is visible in final back/side/three-quarter views.

All six source/model pairs show an ivory skeletal bat with open ribs, vertebral spine, real scapular/pelvic bearings, cyan membranes, separate recessed skull sockets/nasal opening and an open fang-lined jaw. The skeletal rider has the original dark blue hood and fitted dark cloth with pale steel armor, rather than the previous nearly white icy body. Whole seated rider joints, carved skull and held source gear remain joined throughout the native assembly.

All six source/model pairs show the original timber flying chassis: open pilot compartment, plank walls, tan wooden sail wings with wood/iron struts, fitted iron front plate, bronze/leather corner rails and rivets, rear diagonal braces and deep bored side engines. The brown hooded green pilot is crouched within the frame with source ears, leather clothing and whole crossbow. The complete upper body moved with the seated hips and arms; the source compartment and engine depth replace the earlier generic mount.

All six final source/model pairs show the prismatic purple bat with three broad attached turquoise front diamonds at brow/wing roots and the matching broad rear diamond. The final visibility correction moves the real crystal shapes out of the previously buried cranium/wing/back surfaces while preserving physical attachment. The brown hooded green rider has source ears, fitted brown leather clothing and whole short blade; continuous bat body, natural hind joints, wing bones and caudal root resolve the old generic anatomy.

All six final source/model pairs show the large storm-wing bat king with dark continuous body, broad red torn membranes, curved gold temple horns, source forehead armor, red layered chest caparison and physical gold chest chains. The crowned green rider keeps the brown strapped vest, fitted red tiered rear mantle and whole held axe. Complete rider seating and anatomical hind legs/wing roots replace the previous disconnected forms; authored boss height retains the immutable V5 minimum.

All six final source/model pairs show a dark bat with actual hollow ivory mount skull mask, separate real mask eye openings, bone wing leading structures and darker taupe membranes matching the source sails. The hanging green scout has the second distinct carved skull mask, brown hood/body/skirt and physical side packs, whole short weapon and contacting brown suspension harness. Entire suspended upper body, hips and limbs form a joined source assembly rather than displaced boots.

All six final source/model pairs show the eclipse bat's purple body and dusty pink/violet scalloped membranes, source broad open silver crescent wing-root guards, anatomical wing/hind leg interfaces and physical tack. The rider has the deep purple steel cap with continuous contacting temples/cheeks and silver brow/rim, brown leather front/rear vest beneath the silver collar, and a whole purple spear with attached crescent pennant seal. The final source material fix applies to actual exposed fitted plates, so the source brown vest remains visible in front and rear views.

All six final pairs show the grey-purple rift wolf with shaped snout, recessed eyes, natural canine joints/paws, bushy curled tail, source grey dorsal armor and purple back shards. Its brown strapped rider has the dark hood/ears, source spiked grey shoulder equipment, seated whole body and reins. The final source weapon repair replaces the generic spear head with a real connected forged fork and physically seated purple crystal, visible in front/back/side views.

All six final pairs show the thunder manta's continuous flattened curved trunk, rolled cephalic front fins, real long recessed mouth, rectangular recessed eyes, broad swept pectoral fins and long tapering stinging tail. The real fitted overlapping dorsal armor has outward positive-Z thickness and raised caps, replacing previously inward/buried relief; source ivory angular wing runes are physically seated on the fin surface. The source red-masked rider keeps a dark hood, brown strapped vest, whole spear/crimson pennant and joined seated body; hidden depth and camera differences remain authored estimates.

All six final pairs show the Hollow Sky King as a true skeletal creature rather than a generic humanoid: real open ribs surrounding the captive green-faced hooded soul and turquoise heart, exposed curved neck/vertebrae, an angular skull with real sockets and open fang-lined lower jaw, swept horn/bone features, grey overlapping back plates and articulated curled armored tail. Source ragged taupe wings and real jointed bone toes are present. Apertures remain physically open and recessed; boss height remains at least the V5 baseline.

All six final pairs show the fire bat with dark body, orange membranes, fitted riveted metal forehead/cheek/belly/wing-root armor, anatomical toes and real wing shoulder/elbow/wrist. The source dark cap has contacting temple/cheek steel and orange rune, with a brown rear vest and crimson pennant. The final physical pike has a real iron diamond blade with attached orange diamond rune in place of the generic gold tip; whole rider and weapon assemblies remain seated and connected.

All six final pairs show the two distinct green drummers in brown fitted outfits, steel caps, independent seated hips/thighs and arms, beside the actual timber barrel drum with hide heads, steel hoops/staves, skull motif, straps and four whole gripping mallets. The dark bat has red membranes, source ears/nose, continuous torso, real hind joints and wing bones. The former second drummer head gap and missing second-rider scope were resolved through real cervical/body fitting and both complete measured joint chains.

All six final pairs show the Last Howl wolf's dark continuous body, real natural canine joints/paws, curled shaggy tail, fitted fur flank locks and source ivory canine mask with separate recessed red sockets, carved nasal aperture, swept skull ridges and real jaw teeth. The rider has a rounded steel cap, brown outfit, source axe, two actual outer-surface-fitted brown shaggy mantle layers and a strapped back banner with folded red cloth/black wolf insignia. The final mantle correction removes oversized steel shoulder spikes and stale straight rear straps that occluded the hide; the dark/light brown pointed fur layers are visible from the final back/side/three-quarter views.

All six final pairs show the bat thieves with a dark hood, brown strapped outfit, two short physical daggers, two folded red head-owned scarf streamers and attached gold bells with real open undersides/metal suspension. The source red membranes, purple dark animal body, actual wing roots, toes and fitted source tack replace the generic creature. Scarf roots now follow the whole head assembly and bell supports meet actual thorax surfaces.

All six final source/model pairs show Bernhard on the redesigned dark dragon with exactly two canonical hind legs, a tall curved neck with overlapping light steel-grey throat plates, angular plated snout/jaw, recessed amber eyes, three swept horn pairs with amber insets, dark overlapping scales, bronze strapped chest plates, burnt-orange scalloped wings and a long curled armored tail with orange tip. The crouched dark rider has a whole gold-guarded sword with attached orange flame/rune strips, reins and a physical ornate strapped back throne/tower with finials, skull and chain ensemble visible from the rear. Source identity replaces the generic four-legged mount; physical source contacts and authored V5 boss height are retained. After the final metadata-only scope repair, I personally reopened all six newly rendered source/model rows again: the same geometry, charcoal rider cloth, colors, whole sword and source identity remain intact. The physical cloth audit now selects the actual overlapping mantle and skirt meshes while retaining the historical cape record.
